note: T5b-Y4 and T7-P1 (the owner's decisions of 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14; SPEC-multigraph-envelope.md section 3): the /search answer budget, mode plain: the rows alone (MATCHES). What a /search holds is priced while it is built, against --search-max-answer-memory-mb (4,096 MiB by default, staging's; 1 on the recording server so that the sample stays short; 0 = none): the values of each unit, one FASTA record on one pair (its rows and their per-position values as they grow, then its rows as they are handed over: a values account a unit); each unit's own JSON object, checked alone before it is built; and the request's JSON answer, its text and the transport's and the cache's copies (one answer account a request). Without the request field partial_refusal, a unit past the bound refuses the WHOLE request 400, on a multi-graph server too (no pair is named, no envelope), nothing partial sent: {error, account, code: "search_answer_too_large", max_memory_mb}, written in this order (error first, as the intake refusals and resolve_answer_too_large). account is "values" when some unit's values pass the bound, else "answer" (a unit's own object or the request's answer; the units still running then search on, their values only, so that the account never depends on the order the work ran in); here "answer": a unit's own object was priced past the bound before it was built, its values within it (each unit's object, 2,000 rows, past 1 MiB alone). The text is the same in every mode and on every route mode (abundance_sum, align); its advice: fewer top_labels, a larger discovery_fraction, fewer or shorter FASTA records, or no per-position values. A refused request is not cached: the same request is refused again. A request whose work fails for another reason after a unit passed is this refusal. With partial_refusal the units past the bound are answered alone (samples 71-75). Below the bound every answer is the one without a budget, byte for byte. GET /capabilities states the bound (sample 12: multigraph.search; a single-graph server's top-level search). A real run: two copies of a pair whose 2,000 columns share one 100 bp stretch (the service's top_labels 10,000 case: each pair answers 2,000 rows), the request that stretch; at the default bound the same request answered 200 (846,676 bytes of text, the answer account 4,665,424 B, the values account at most 66,272 B a unit).
